newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks inch up, looking at Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks inch up, looking at Wall Street.

text.p: Mexican stocks edged up in early trade on Friday after ziz-zagging in an uncertain reaction to U.S. financial markets and under apprehension over what was expected to be a bad day for the peso, traders said.

"Most stocks are opening flat and at thin volume, apart from some hefty cross trades. The Dow (Jones) took us by surprise," a floor trader said, saying higher U.S. long bond yields had led many to expect the Dow Jones would open down.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was up 0.80 points, or 0.02 percent in the opening minutes of trade, at 4,120.33. The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 20.17 points at 7,325.46.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was off 9/32 to yield 6.90 percent following what dealers said were strong U.S. jobs data for May.
Trading volume .TV.MX of 18.6 million shares was inflated by cross trades, three of which accounted for more than 11 million shares.
"It's very dull, nothing much is happening. And although it does not cause much concern, the weak peso is slowing down the market," a desk trader said.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts had meanwhile opened 0.7 of a centavo weaker at 7.9695/7.9750 per dollar.

Dealers said financial firm Bancomer constributed most to market gains, with its B class shares up eight centavos to 3.41 pesos. The A class was more active, but mainly due to cross trades, they said.
Telecomms firm Telmex, down two centavos to 18.48 pesos, weighed down most on the market.
On the broad market, of 46 stocks traded, gainers balanced sliders, of which there were 17 each.
